subject: Linguistics
title: Design Features of Language
description: A micro-lesson that makes Design Features of Language usable.

hook.text: In 1960 Charles Hockett listed thirteen features that define human language.

buildup.text: Some features—like using sound—are shared with animal calls.

discovery.text: But duality of patterning is almost uniquely human: meaningless sounds combine into meaningful words.

twist.text: Sign languages prove the channel doesn't matter—hands work as well as vocal cords.

climax.text: The features cluster together: any system missing several of them isn't a full language.

punchline.text: Language is a package deal—no single trick defines it.

quiz.question: What does duality of patterning mean?
options: Meaningless units combine into meaningful ones
